policy_title: Scrap Draconian Anti-Protest Laws and Halt Facial Recognition Surveillance
stated: Scrap the Conservatives’ draconian anti-protest laws, restoring preexisting protections for both peaceful assembly and public safety, and immediately halt the use of live facial recognition surveillance by the police and private companies.

source.quote: Scrap the Conservatives’ draconian anti-protest laws, restoring preexisting protections for both peaceful assembly and public safety, and immediately halt the use of live facial recognition surveillance by the police and private companies.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets civil liberties (right to peaceful assembly/protest and privacy from surveillance), which are core O9 rights and freedoms indicators.

Halting live facial recognition removes a tool police use to identify wanted suspects, and relaxing protest restrictions changes public-order management — both have a concrete, non-negligible effect on crime-detection rates and public-order indicators under O5.

Both components directly expand negative liberty: scrapping anti-protest laws restores freedom of expression and assembly, while halting live facial recognition removes a form of mass surveillance — both are core O10 indicators.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O10 improves (the explicit purpose — rolling back coercive and surveillance powers) and O5 potentially worsens (loss of enforcement capability — the concrete tradeoff the policy's critics would name). No other fundamental earns a non-negligible verdict: the equal-treatment/democratic-rights angle on protest sits squarely in O10 per the boundary notes; there is no direct fiscal, housing, health, or labour-market mechanism.
